text: A set $\alpha$ is an ordinal exactly when it is well-ordered by $\in$ and, in addition, is:
explanation: The chapter defines an ordinal as a transitive set that is well-ordered by $\in$. Ordinals need not be finite ($\omega$ is infinite); every cardinal is an ordinal but not conversely (e.g. $\omega+1$ is an ordinal that is not a cardinal); and complementation is not a well-defined operation here.
